One `guide@operator-name` login serves all guides for this operator, based on its subdomain, and stays the same after a subdomain rename.

After setup, guides use that username and password on the normal sign-in screen and go directly to [Guide Simple View](/simpleguide). The roll call shows expected passenger totals, client contact links and check-ins. **Trip photos** on a departure opens the same Photos workspace as the full dashboard: image/video uploads through the operator's connected Google Drive, individual or bulk photo links, recent galleries, and **Send photos and thank you email**. Confirming sends the existing photo/thank-you email and WhatsApp photo message to eligible lead bookers for that trip. Guides cannot open office or marketing settings, create bookings, record payments, change the Drive connection or choose arbitrary recipients. This is separate from adding an ordinary dashboard admin and from the existing /guide check-in app.

Use **Disable guide access** or **Enable guide access** to change availability. **Get fresh password setup link** replaces the prior link and requires the shared password to be set again, including when it is forgotten. Do not ask guides to share passwords or private setup tokens in chat.

title: Settings — Tours & Activities
content:
Settings — Tours & Activities
## Tours & Activities

Create and edit tours, descriptions, duration, departure schedules, default capacity, base and peak prices, images and confirmation taglines. Drag to reorder the booking-site cards. Activate/deactivate and show/hide control sales and public visibility; neither action cancels existing bookings. Tours with booking history or linked active vouchers cannot be deleted.

Departure times use a **24-hour clock** in the operator’s saved timezone (SAST for South Africa). Type **1800** continuously to enter **18:00**, or **0930** for **09:30**, without selecting AM/PM. For a **2-hour, 30-minute** tour, select **hours**, enter **2**, and enter **30** in the adjacent minutes field. Existing durations load into the matching hours and minutes when edited; whole-day tours still support **days**.

When generating slots, choose **Date range** for a repeating weekday schedule or **Specific dates** to pick individual tour dates. Add as many dates and departure times as needed. Each departure time is created on every selected date, and existing departures are skipped. For a new tour, the selected schedule is generated when you choose **Add Tour**; for an existing tour, choose **Generate Slots**.

**Last-minute deals** have a deal price and a start/end window measured in hours before departure. They apply to eligible unsold availability, not refunds on an existing paid booking. Upcoming departure-time bundles can also be managed here; [Slots](/slots) has the full calendar and bulk tools.

**Custom Booking Questions** is in [Tours & Activities](/settings#tours). Add a template or a question, choose its answer type, options and required status, then save. The answers are captured with the booking and shown to staff; these questions are not in Booking Site Configuration.

title: Settings — Booking Add-Ons
content:
Settings — Booking Add-Ons
## Booking Add-Ons

Optional extras customers can add at checkout (photo packages, equipment hire). Create, edit, and drag-reorder.

title: Settings — Booking Site Configuration
content:
Settings — Booking Site Configuration
## Booking Site Configuration

Your customer-facing booking site's policies, directions, branding, background and hero text, navigation, button and footer copy, theme colours, contact links, timezone, chatbot avatar and cancellation policy tiers. The booking-site preview shows the effect of the settings, including theme text contrast. Custom checkout questions are maintained under Tours & Activities.

title: Settings — Embed Widget
content:
Settings — Embed Widget
## Embed Widget

A copyable snippet to embed your booking widget on your own website.

title: Settings — Email Customisation
content:
Settings — Email Customisation
## Email Customisation

Per-email-type colour themes and banner images for the emails customers receive (confirmations, invoices, cancellations, photos, and so on).

title: Settings — Operations & AI Configuration
content:
Settings — Operations & AI Configuration
## Operations & AI Configuration

Arrival instructions, what to bring and wear, FAQ answers, and the AI chatbot's personality and business knowledge. This content feeds the customer website and WhatsApp assistant; arrival and packing instructions also feed guest emails. It does not change the dashboard help assistant's product guide. Staff with the **Booking Site Config** grant can also manage this section and Embed Widget.

title: Settings — WhatsApp Bot Mode
content:
Settings — WhatsApp Bot Mode
## WhatsApp Bot Mode

Controls WhatsApp auto-replies: **Always**, **Outside business hours**, or **Never**. Outside-hours mode uses the saved weekly schedule and business timezone. Human takeover on an individual conversation still takes precedence. This section requires a main admin; ordinary Settings grants do not unlock it.

title: Simple View, roll call and check-ins
content:
Simple View, roll call and check-ins
Choose **Simple View** in the full dashboard's header for the phone and tablet operations workflow. Its navigation has **Today**, **Add walk-in** and **Full dashboard**. **Full dashboard** returns to / for scheduling, refunds, marketing and configuration.

title: Simple View, roll call and check-ins — Today and Calendar
content:
Simple View, roll call and check-ins — Today and Calendar
## Today and Calendar

[Today](/simple) opens **Roll call** for the current business date. Use the arrows or date picker for another day. [Calendar](/simple/calendar) also shows that selected day's booked sessions in time order. These screens show sessions with bookings, not every empty departure in the full Slots calendar.

Each session shows its time, activity, booked and arrived guests, and available places or a Full, Closed, Cancelled or Departed label. Its roll call shows each lead booker and arrival count. The count appears beside the name as **2/2**, followed by **Edit**, which opens that session's check-ins to adjust arrivals. Contact details appear as **WhatsApp**, **Call** and **Email** buttons instead of phone numbers or email addresses. WhatsApp and Call require a valid phone number; Email requires a valid email address. The same buttons are available on payment-recovery rows. South African local numbers are converted to +27 automatically. You write and send the message yourself.

Simple View updates automatically when bookings change, every minute, when the connection returns, and when you return to the browser window. There is no timezone/update row or Refresh day button.

title: Simple View, roll call and check-ins — Payment and waiver readiness
content:
Simple View, roll call and check-ins — Payment and waiver readiness
## Payment and waiver readiness

[Check-ins](/simple/check-ins) shows the payment and waiver status before recording arrivals. If money has actually been received offline, choose **Cash**, **EFT**, **Card (terminal)** or **Other**, add a payment note or reference, and record it. Wait for the refreshed booking to confirm payment. A pay-on-arrival exception alone is not a recorded payment.

A signed waiver and payment in full are required before adding arrivals in Simple View. Account/reseller approval and Allow Without Payment do not bypass this requirement. Check the displayed blocking reason if the control is unavailable. Correcting an existing arrival count downward remains possible. Recording a payment does not collect a card payment through Yoco.

title: Simple View, roll call and check-ins — Partial group arrivals
content:
Simple View, roll call and check-ins — Partial group arrivals
## Partial group arrivals

Use the minus/plus controls to set the number actually present, from zero up to the booked group size, then save. For example, record 2 of 4 arrived when half the party is present. Correct a mistaken arrival count here as well. The Today/Calendar roll-call checkbox marks the whole eligible group present or resets a fully present group; use Check-ins for precise partial counts.

title: Simple View, roll call and check-ins — Walk-ins and the shared demo
content:
Simple View, roll call and check-ins — Walk-ins and the shared demo
## Walk-ins and the shared demo

Choose **Add walk-in** in the header. The form at /simple/new-booking carries the selected date or departure. Use the **X** beside the Add walk-in heading to close the form and return to the screen and date you came from. Review the adult/child counts, extras, payment action and any required booking or participant questions before choosing Create. Draft details survive closing, Back and Cancel within the same authenticated browser tab. Capacity and normal booking checks still apply.

The shared demo explains operations without committing payments, arrivals or new bookings. Use the full dashboard's AI bot for its product tour.

title: Simple View, roll call and check-ins — Guide-only access
content:
Simple View, roll call and check-ins — Guide-only access
## Guide-only access

Guides use the operator's shared `guide@operator-name` login and chosen password. This opens [Guide Simple View](/simpleguide) directly, with the roll call, client contact buttons, expected passenger counts and check-ins for the selected day. Use the date arrows or date picker to choose a day; its data refreshes automatically. **Trip photos** opens the same Photos workspace as the main dashboard, preselected for that departure. Guides can upload images/videos, paste or bulk-import links, review recent photo links, and confirm **Send photos and thank you email** to notify that trip's lead bookers. Access is limited to the guide's operator; Full dashboard, walk-ins, payment recording and marketing campaigns remain unavailable.

The operator owner sets up this login in [Settings → Admin Users → Guide login](/settings#admins), chooses **Create guide login**, and privately shares the one-use password setup link. It expires after 48 hours. A guide chooses the shared password once and is signed directly into Simple View. After that, all guides use the shared username and password on the normal sign-in screen. The owner can disable access or issue a fresh setup link when the password is forgotten. Shared guides can send trip photos and the existing thank-you email for their own operator's trips.

title: Slots
content:
Slots
Slots are your bookable departures: a tour at a time on a date with a capacity and price. Customers can only book where an OPEN slot exists.

title: Slots — Creating slots
content:
Slots — Creating slots
## Creating slots

Open [Slots](/slots) and choose **Add Slot**. The **Add New Slots** dialog asks for the tour, start time, one or more date ranges, capacity and an optional price override. Blank price uses the tour default. Existing departures at the same tour and time are skipped rather than duplicated.

For repeating schedules choose **Bulk Generate**: select one or more tours, date ranges, departure times, weekdays and capacity. Review the per-tour overrides and preview before generating. Results show created slots, skipped duplicates and errors for each tour.

Generating slots adds missing departures. Changing the weekday selection does not close or remove departures that were generated earlier.

title: Slots — Calendar views
content:
Slots — Calendar views
## Calendar views

Switch between **Week** and **Day**, use the arrows or date picker, or choose **Month** to open the monthly booking overview. Month helps you jump to a date; slot editing happens in the day or week calendar.

title: Slots — Editing a slot
content:
Slots — Editing a slot
## Editing a slot

The **Edit Slot** modal changes time, capacity, or price. It deliberately does not change status — opening, closing, and cancelling are separate actions so a price edit can never accidentally cancel a departure.

title: Slots — Open, close, cancel — the difference
content:
Slots — Open, close, cancel — the difference
## Open, close, cancel — the difference

- **Close** — stops new bookings but keeps existing ones. Use when a departure is full enough or you want to pause sales.
- **Reopen** — makes a closed slot bookable again.
- **Cancel & notify** or **Weather cancel** in a slot's dialog cancels its active bookings and sends cancellation notices. Weather cancellation gives eligible paid guests reschedule, voucher or full-refund choices even at short notice. Refunds are not automatically completed by cancellation.
- **Cancel Day(s)** applies weather cancellation across selected dates. Select the date headers in the calendar first, then review the confirmation and choose **Cancel Everything**.
- **Reopen Day(s)** opens closed departures on selected dates for new bookings. Reopening a departure does not restore previously cancelled bookings.

Cancelling a whole departure or selected days uses the main-admin cancellation service and requires MAIN_ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN. Operations staff should ask their main admin to perform it. Closing sales and editing a slot are separate actions.

title: Slots — Bulk edit
content:
Slots — Bulk edit
## Bulk edit

Choose **Bulk Edit** to open **Bulk Edit Slots**. Apply a new capacity, price and/or time across a date range for one tour or all tours. Blank fields keep their existing values; enter **NULL** in the price field to reset to the tour default. Editing time, capacity or price does not cancel bookings.

To make existing availability **weekends only**, choose the tour (or **All Tours**) and the date range, then choose **Close weekday slots**. Review the number of future Monday–Friday slots and confirm. Weekdays use the operator's timezone. Saturday and Sunday slots, existing bookings and holds are preserved; this does not cancel trips, refund payments or message guests. The capacity, price and time fields are ignored by this action. For future slot generation, select only Saturday and Sunday.

title: Slots — Hidden slots
content:
Slots — Hidden slots
## Hidden slots

By default, CLOSED and zero-capacity slots are hidden from the list. Use the "Show closed / 0-capacity" toggle to reveal them.

title: Slots — Peak pricing on slots
content:
Slots — Peak pricing on slots
## Peak pricing on slots

Slots carry peak flags and price overrides that are managed from the Peak Pricing page — a slot inside an active peak period shows its peak price automatically.

title: Super Admin
content:
Super Admin
Super Admin is your platform control room. It can access every business. Never give this role to a client.

title: Super Admin — Before handing a client their booking link
content:
Super Admin — Before handing a client their booking link
## Before handing a client their booking link

Open **Client readiness & support** and expand their business. Automatic checks show whether the owner account, subscription, policies, activity, future availability and provider settings exist. “Saved” does not mean a payment or message worked.

Perform the six client tests and record only what you actually verified. Every confirmation has an actor and timestamp in the audit trail. The checklist is not an automatic launch approval: unresolved support problems still need attention.

If billing or policies are missing, use **Complete missing setup** once. It creates only missing records from today, preserves existing records, and does not send an invoice or take money.

**Add New Client** creates the business and Main Admin immediately. If that operator should finish the guided wizard, enter the same booking subdomain and Main Admin email under **Onboarding Invites**. The invite attaches to the existing business; it does not create a second one. The booking site pauses until the operator completes the wizard. Businesses with bookings cannot use this handoff; their owners finish setup in the admin dashboard. For a new operator, you can start directly with **Onboarding Invites**, which creates a fenced skeleton business. A retried assisted submission uses the same request ID to avoid duplicates.

In **Business Management**, an operator still marked **ONBOARDING** has an **Activate operator** action. Complete missing setup under **Client readiness & support**, check launch readiness, then activate and record a reason. This changes the operator and its subscription to **ACTIVE**, enables online bookings, and records the change in the audit trail. It does not complete the guided wizard or send the owner a password setup email; use **Send setup link** if needed.

Under a business's **Admin Users**, choose **Edit contact details** to update an administrator's name, email and optional phone number, including the Main Admin. Saving an email changes the existing account's sign-in address immediately and expires old setup links. The account, password and permissions are kept. Use **Send setup link** afterward if password setup is still pending. Main Admins have the same contact editor for their own business in **Settings → Admin Users**.

title: Super Admin — Support and staff access
content:
Super Admin — Support and staff access
## Support and staff access

Select the client before opening their settings, billing, privacy requests or notifications. The server verifies the selected business against your sign-in; ordinary clients cannot switch into another business by editing a request.

In the client's detail panel, **Send setup link** emails a secure password link. Let the owner choose their password. **Suspend** blocks staff access and revokes refresh sessions without deleting records. **Reactivate** requires an available seat. You cannot suspend yourself, another platform account, or the last active Main Admin. Increase seats or promote another active Main Admin first, as appropriate.

Business suspension requires confirmation and an audit reason. It stops trading and is not automatically lifted just because an invoice is paid. Pausing/resuming billing and changing seats update billing records atomically. Seat reductions cannot fall below active staff.

title: Super Admin — Operator settings support
content:
Super Admin — Operator settings support
## Operator settings support

Open **Operator settings support** at /super-admin/sensitive-actions. Select the operator first to change its banking, WhatsApp or Yoco settings. Changes use your signed-in Super Admin account and are recorded in the audit trail. Credential status does not expose saved secret values.

MFA has been removed for all accounts, including Super Admins. Banking, integration credentials, platform settings and client onboarding use normal sign-in with the existing role permissions. No authenticator setup, QR code or six-digit authenticator code is required.

title: Super Admin — Monthly invoices
content:
Super Admin — Monthly invoices
## Monthly invoices

Use **Platform Invoices** for operator billing. The email usage panel is a usage/pricing view; email overage is included once in the platform invoice, not in a second customer invoice.

The preview and generated invoice share one calculation: plan, seat history, active days, email overage and AI overage. Review a draft before sending it. Generating a draft does not charge a card; sending it sends a real email and can create a payment link.

For a wrong unpaid draft without a payment link, use **Void draft**, give a reason, correct the source settings, then generate a replacement for the same month. The old document stays in **Voided history**. Paid documents are not editable or voidable here.

If a payment link exists or checkout creation started, correction is blocked until provider cancellation is verified. The Checkout API does not expose a documented cancellation operation in the reviewed API reference. Do not create a second payable invoice or delete the first to get around this protection; arrange cancellation/reconciliation with Yoco and platform support.

**Mark Paid** is for money you have actually received. Check the amount and reference in your bank first. If an old payment link has already been shared, arrange its cancellation as well so the client cannot accidentally pay twice.

title: Super Admin — Daily monitoring in plain English
content:
Super Admin — Daily monitoring in plain English
## Daily monitoring in plain English

Sentry tells you when software reports a problem. It does not replace checking that customers actually received messages or money.

1. Open [Sentry errors](https://bookingtours.sentry.io/issues/?environment=production). Select **production**, **Unresolved** and the last 24 hours.
2. Open new or repeating issues. Copy the issue link; note first/last seen, event count and tags. **app** identifies admin, booking or edge. **business_id** identifies a client when available; **function.name** identifies an edge service.
3. Prioritise payment/refund failures, sign-in failures, any wrong-client information and missed scheduled jobs. Use this page's support counts to find the affected client. Do not blindly repeat a payment, refund or message.
4. Send the issue link, client name and a plain-English description to your developer. Resolve the issue only after a deployed fix has been checked. “Regressed” means a previously resolved problem returned.

Open [Sentry monitors](https://bookingtours.sentry.io/monitors/) and check **Booking cleanup and reminders**. It should start every five minutes and report completion. A missed/failed run needs investigation even if customers have not complained.

Check the control room and Sentry at the start and end of every day, after each onboarding, and after a release. Production new/regressed-error and error-spike rules route to the platform owner's Sentry account. A test alert must actually arrive before email monitoring is considered proven.

The included cron monitor covers cleanup/reminders. Marketing functions report returned failures to Sentry, but have no separate missed-run monitor in this release. Sentry is not an independent website uptime check; if the whole site or telemetry is unavailable, inspect the hosting dashboard and public booking page.

Sources: [Sentry cron monitoring](https://docs.sentry.io/product/monitors-and-alerts/monitors/crons/), [Sentry issue triage](https://docs.sentry.io/product/issues/states-triage/), [Yoco Checkout API](https://developer.yoco.com/api-reference/checkout-api/checkout/create-checkout).

title: Vouchers
content:
Vouchers
Open [Marketing](/marketing), then the **Vouchers** tab at /vouchers. Vouchers cover gifts, credits and tour redemption. Each has a code the customer uses when booking with your business. The create form generates an 8-character code and lets you regenerate or edit it.

title: Vouchers — Creating a voucher
content:
Vouchers — Creating a voucher
## Creating a voucher

Fill in the recipient and buyer details, choose the tour, and pick the type:

- **Gift** — bought by one person for another, with an optional gift message.
- **Credit** — a monetary amount the recipient can spend on a booking.
- **Free Trip** — a voucher for tour redemption. The dashboard create form still sells it by payment link; selecting this type does not grant unpaid complimentary credit.

Enter a positive rand value and a buyer email, choose the type, and review the buyer, recipient, tour and optional gift message. **Send payment link** emails the buyer a checkout link. Every voucher sold through this form remains PENDING until payment is confirmed. Expiry is set to three years automatically, and the list shows its date.

Recipient email is optional and controls gift delivery. Credit vouchers arising from cancellations or booking changes are a separate recovery flow; creating an order here does not complete a refund.

title: Vouchers — Gift voucher photos and messages
content:
Vouchers — Gift voucher photos and messages
## Gift voucher photos and messages

1. Open **Settings → Tours & Activities** and edit the experience.
2. Under **Gift voucher photo**, choose **Upload voucher photo** and select a JPG, PNG or WebP up to 5 MB.
3. Open **Preview gift voucher** to check the photo with sample details, then save the tour. **Use tour image** removes the separate voucher photo; if neither photo is set, the gift voucher default photo is used.

When creating a voucher, choose the experience under **Gift voucher photo**, enter the recipient and buyer names, and add a **Gift message**. Check the preview before sending the payment link: the names, amount, experience and personal message appear on the photo, with message line breaks preserved. Customers buying online can also choose an experience photo and preview their personal message.

The selected design appears on the confirmation page and gift emails, with the voucher code and expiry after payment. Choosing a photo changes the appearance only; it does not change where the voucher can be redeemed. Updating an experience’s photo affects new vouchers; existing purchases keep their selected photo.

title: WhatsApp and automatic messages
content:
WhatsApp and automatic messages
BookingTours messages your customers automatically at the right moments — this explains what goes out, when, and the WhatsApp rules that govern it.

title: WhatsApp and automatic messages — What's sent automatically
content:
WhatsApp and automatic messages — What's sent automatically
## What's sent automatically

- **Booking confirmation** — on successful payment, with the invoice.
- **Payment link follow-up** — if an online checkout was started but not paid, the customer is emailed their payment link after the hold lapses.
- **Trip reminders** — before the trip, WhatsApp-first with waiver links bundled where applicable, falling back to email.
- **Review requests** — after the trip.
- **Cancellation notices** — when you cancel slots (weather or otherwise), with self-service reschedule/voucher/refund options.

Automatic jobs track sent messages and retries to avoid duplicate scheduled delivery. A queued job or successful submission is not proof of delivery; failed WhatsApp and transactional email jobs can be inspected in [Broadcasts → Failed Notifications](/notifications) by a main admin. Trip timing uses your business timezone.

title: WhatsApp and automatic messages — The WhatsApp 24-hour rule
content:
WhatsApp and automatic messages — The WhatsApp 24-hour rule
## The WhatsApp 24-hour rule

WhatsApp allows free-form business messages only within 24 hours of the customer's last message. Outside that window, only pre-approved templates can be sent; other messages queue as "waiting for window" and send once the customer messages in. This is a WhatsApp platform rule that applies to every business.

title: WhatsApp and automatic messages — The WhatsApp bot
content:
WhatsApp and automatic messages — The WhatsApp bot
## The WhatsApp bot

The AI assistant can answer customer WhatsApp messages automatically — controlled by the WhatsApp Bot Mode section in Settings (always, outside business hours, or never). Conversations the bot can't handle land in your Inbox marked as needing a reply.

title: WhatsApp and automatic messages — When WhatsApp fails
content:
WhatsApp and automatic messages — When WhatsApp fails
## When WhatsApp fails

The Failed Notifications tab under Broadcasts tracks WhatsApp failures and transactional email jobs. Important workflows can fall back to email where configured and valid contact details exist. Review the returned outcome and failure log rather than assuming every guest was reached.
